diagnoses.summary: High SPE with coherent T2 elevation and dominant contribution from CSTR H2 vent (PCV) and CSTR pressure. Rule-based hypotheses point to a PCV-related fault causing reactor pressure rise and abnormal vent behavior.
PCA shows a large, coherent upset with major reactor pressure increase; evidence points to H2 vent/PCV issues causing high CSTR pressure.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent upset driven by reactor pressure rise and hydrogen vent behavior, with strongest evidence pointing to an H2 PCV fault causing restricted venting and pressure buildup.

PCA indicates a large coherent upset with reactor pressure rising and a strong contribution from the CSTR pressure measurement and the H2 vent flow. Alarms show high reactor pressure. Likely H2 PCV fault causing insufficient relief.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong contribution from CSTR pressure and H2 vent flow, accompanied by high reactor pressure alarms. The most consistent fault is an obstructed or stuck H2 PCV, causing reactor pressure to rise and the controller to compensate. Other plausible but less likely faults involve PCV capacity degradation or a biased pressure sensor.
PCA abnormal with coherent process upset dominated by CSTR pressure rise and H2 vent control mismatch; most likely a PCV actuator fault causing restricted venting and pressure buildup.

The PCA shows a large, coherent upset dominated by reactor pressure rise driven by the H2 vent system. Alarms indicate high reactor pressure. Top contributors point to CSTR pressure and H2 vent flow changes, with the PCV (H2 vent) being central. This points to a PCV fault causing pressure buildup.

PCA flags a large, coherent process upset with concurrent high pressure and high SPE, dominated by the CSTR pressure signal and H2 vent activity. Alarms indicate reactor pressure is high. Most consistent with a faulty H2 PCV (actuator) either stuck closed or degraded capacity, causing pressure buildup.

PCA flags a large, coherent process upset with strong reactor pressure rise and PCV-related symptoms. High T2 and high SPE indicate a significant, but structurally coherent disturbance, not a random sensor fault. The strongest rule-based hypotheses center on the hydrogen purge (H2 PCV) side of the reactor relief/vent system, with PCV-side faults most consistent with the observed pressure excursion and related controller activity.

PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with major pressure rise in the CSTR and high H2 vent activity. Alarms on cstr_pressure_bar (R_P_H, R_P_HH) and a saturated RB_LIC loop output point to an H2 vent/valve issue driving a pressure rise with compensating loops fighting the upset.
PCA anomaly with coherent upset dominated by reactor pressure rise and PCV influence; high T2 and large SPE indicate a coherent process upset with strong PCV-related effect and possible PCV fault.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations and a saturated RB_LIC loop. The most consistent fault is a biased reactor pressure sensor, with plausible additional faults in condenser cooling and PCV/system upsets contributing to the disturbance.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations. The strongest evidence centers on the CSTR pressure reading being anomalous (high T² contribution) and a saturated RB_LIC loop, with TOP_TIC actively compensating. This pattern is most consistent with a biased/failed pressure sensor (sensor fault) driving the abnormal correlations, possibly with related PCV/flow issues.

PCA shows a large coherent upset with strong pressure and holdup changes, dominated by CSTR pressure and holdup signals, with PCV-related fault hypotheses highest. The evidence points to H2 PCV (vent valve) issues affecting reactor pressure control, most likely capacity degradation or being stuck, rather than a pure sensor fault.

PCA shows a large, coherent process upset with significant deviation in reactor pressure-related variables and PCV control signals. The most likely root causes are faults in the H2 PCV (valve) related to capacity degradation or being stuck closed, causing abnormal reactor pressure response and compensatory loop action.

PCA shows large coherent upset with both Hotelling T² and SPE violations, with reactor pressure (cstr_pressure_bar) being the dominant contributor and pushing toward the high alarm, while the controller output for reactor pressure (R_PIC) remains near baseline. This pattern, plus the rule-based hypotheses, points to a problem with the hydrogen purge/vent path (H2 PCV) causing pressure rise and abnormal correlations.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with both T2 and SPE active, dominated by the H2 PCV control loop. The most consistent faults are PCV actuator issues under H2 vent valve (PCV). Upstream measurements (reactor pressure) are elevated and the PIC loop is saturated, indicating the PCV is not behaving to the setpoint and is likely limiting flow or failing open/closed behavior.
PCA flags a large coherent upset with PCV/pressure related symptoms; PCV-related actuator faults are most consistent with the evidence, supported by saturation of R_PIC and rising reactor pressure.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with reactor pressure control dominated by H2 PCV (PCV) related disturbances. High T² and high SPE point to a PCV/pressure control issue propagating through the process, with PCV-related faults highlighted as most likely by rule-based hints.

PCA detects a large, coherent upset with reactor pressure rising and PCV/valve loops saturated. Likely issues involve the H2 PCV and its associated control loops, with possible concurrent condenser/ cooling issues contributing to elevated tray temperatures. At least two actuator loops appear saturated with PVs not moving toward setpoints, pointing to either out-of-range transmitter/controller signals or PCV/valve faults.

PCA detects a coherent plant upset with large shift along normal directions and widespread SPE violations, dominated by the H2 PCV/control loop. The strongest evidence points to a degradation or obstruction in the H2 PCV (PCV capacity degradation or stuck-closed) causing reactor pressure to rise and forcing the PCV control loop to saturate while PV remains off-set.

A coherent plant upset with high T2 and high SPE, with loop saturation on R_PIC and RB_LIC pointing toward a H2 vent valve (PCV) related issue causing abnormal reactor/column conditions. The rule-based hints also align with PCV/measured deviations, suggesting PCV capacity issue rather than a pure sensor fault.

PCA shows a coherent plant upset with large T² and SPE violations, with strong evidence pointing to H2 PCV issues, likely capacity degradation affecting venting and reactor pressure control; condenser cooling loss is a plausible secondary contributor given multiple tray temperatures involved.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong involvement of the H2 PCV actuator loop; the most compelling fault is a PCV/PCV-related issue driving the reactor pressure abnormality, with R_PIC being the primary loop pushing the upset.

PCA abnormal with both T2 and SPE violations; the dominant contributor to SPE is op.R_PIC with its controller output saturated at PV off setpoint, indicating an actuator/controller fault propagating to the process. Several rule-based hypotheses point to R_PIC being out of range, with secondary possibilities related to H2 PCV faults affecting the same loop and condenser cooling effects contributing modestly.

High Hotelling T2 and SPE with saturated control loops, dominated by the H2 PCV-related loop (R_PIC). The evidence points to a faulty H2 PCV actuator, most likely degraded capacity or being stuck, causing reactor pressure issues and prompting compensatory loop action. Multiple faults from the catalogue are plausible but PCV-related failures are most consistent with the data.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong influence from the H2 PCV control loop (R_PIC) and reactor/ CSTR related inventories, consistent with a fault in the H2 PCV (PCV valve actuator) or its capacity, rather than random sensor drift.
High Hotelling T2 and high SPE indicate a coherent upset with PCV (H2 vent) related fault; most likely H2 PCV fault causing reactor pressure control loop to misbehave.
A large, coherent process upset with the R_PIC loop saturated and driving abnormal pressure indicators. Likely H2 PCV / protective valve issues propagating through the CSTR feed and pressure control.

A large, coherent plant upset with reactor pressure rise and a saturated PIC loop strongly points to the Hydrogen PCV (cstr_vent_valve) fault, most likely degradation or sticking, causing insufficient pressure relief and looping saturation.

PCA flags a large, coherent process upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations. Dominant contributions point to the H2 PCV control path (R_PIC) affecting reactor pressure and CSTR outlet pressure, with loop saturation hints and a high SPE suggesting an actuator fault rather than a pure sensor drift.

High T2 and SPE with a dominant SPE contributor from op.R_PIC and saturated R_PIC loop suggests a fault at the reactor pressure control/measurement path. The most likely fault is that the R_PIC output is out of its normal range, i.e., R_PIC_out_of_range.

The PCA signals a large, coherent upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations driven primarily by the R_PIC loop; the most likely faults are problems with the H2 PCV (cstr vent valve) such as capacity degradation or being stuck closed, causing reactor pressure rise and the loop to saturate as it tries to compensate.

PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with both T2 and SPE elevated. The R_PIC controller output is saturated while the reactor pressure is rising, and the cstr_pressure_bar measurement is a major contributor to the SPE.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with both T2 and SPE violated, and the H2 PCV (R_PIC) loop is saturated. The top contributors point to the H2 PCV control path driving reactor pressure aberrations, with CSTR pressure also contributing. This pattern is most consistent with a degraded or stuck PCV that is not opening as commanded, causing reactor pressure to rise and the PI loop to saturate while attempts to compensate propagate through the process.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset dominated by the H2 PCV control loop, with the PCV (R_PIC) saturated and its commanded vs. actual mismatch. This points to a fault in the hydrogen purge/vent valve path rather than a pure sensor issue.

PCA abnormal with both T2 and SPE high, dominated by a large coherent upset likely originating from the hydrogen purge (PCV) subsystem. Upstream saturation on PCV control and reactor pressure signal support a PCV-related fault rather than a pure sensor issue.

The PCA shows a large, coherent plant upset with significant SPE—driven primarily by the H2 PCV control loop (R_PIC) and reactor pressure. The most consistent fault is an H2 PCV actuator issue causing reactor pressure to rise and loop commanded value to be unable to achieve the PV.

PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with simultaneous high T² and high SPE, dominated by the H2 PCV control loop (R_PIC) and reactor pressure/holdup signals. The evidence points to a fault in the H2 PCV (vent valve) causing reactor pressure rise and related CSTR conditions.
